items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: my guitar instructor who is a wonderful guy who still lives in Florida named Jack Peterson

ctx.x: Yeah I think so. I don’t know if I’d attribute it as much to the actual education that I got from specific teachers. I think it was more just the experience of being in school playing and developing and being around teachers and other students. And if anything I would attribute certain things of course to, there were a couple of teachers that were very important to me, Herb Pomeroy was one, he was a wonderful trumpet player but his main job at Berklee was to teach — he taught arranging, he taught advanced…

which were small ensembles of anywhere from like four to maybe six people. It could be a couple of horns for the rhythm section — I was in one that was just guitar and saxophone, piano, bass and drums. And it was wonderful because I had to function like a horn player. And I couldn’t read worth — I was terrible. I mean most guitar players will acknowledge that they, it’s a difficult instrument to read on. So I remember when they would first write tunes on the board and the saxophone player could read quite well.…
What kind of music was in your household when you were growing up as a kid?
